# 1 Clement Chapter 61 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 61

---

## Council Notes

**On "Guardian" / "Advocate" / "Protector" (v.3):** EMET: "Guardian." LOGOS: "Advocate." PNEUMA: "Protector." The Greek *prostasias* means "one who stands before / advocate / protector." This is a key christological title. "High Priest" (all agents agree) is explicit; the second title *prostasias* is: LOGOS "Advocate" follows the legal sense (*pro-* = before + *histēmi* = stand); EMET "Guardian" and PNEUMA "Protector" follow the protective sense. In the context of Christ interceding for souls, "Advocate" (LOGOS) is most theologically precise, echoing 1 John 2:1. Retained.

**On "excellent and unspeakable might" / "magnificent and indescribable dominion" (v.1):** EMET: "excellent and unspeakable might." LOGOS: "magnificent and indescribable dominion." The Greek *megaloprepous kai anexichniastou dynasteias* = magnificent and unsearchable power/dominion. "Magnificent and unsearchable dominion" would be the most literal. "Magnificent and indescribable dominion" (LOGOS) is adopted.

**On prayer for rulers as political theology (v.1–2):** This prayer for civil rulers under Domitian (c.96 CE) is a remarkable political statement — Christians are praying for the very emperor who may be persecuting them. The prayer reflects the theology of Rom 13 and 1 Tim 2. All agents preserve this context.

**On "now and unto all generations and for ever and ever" (v.3):** All agents agree. The doxological formula is one of the earliest examples of the expanded Christian doxology. It should be rendered precisely.

---

**61:1** *You, Master, have given to them the power of sovereignty*
*through your magnificent and indescribable dominion,*
*so that we, knowing the glory and honor you have given them,*
*may be subject to them,*
*resisting nothing in your will.*

*Grant to them, Lord:*
*health, peace, harmony, and stability,*
*that they may administer without offence*
*the authority you have entrusted to them.*

**61:2** *For you, O heavenly Master, King of the ages,*
*give to the sons of men glory and honor and authority*
*over the things upon the earth.*

*Direct their counsel, O Lord,*
*according to what is good and well-pleasing before you,*
*that they may exercise in peace and meekness and piety*
*the authority given to them by you,*
*and so obtain your mercy.*

**61:3** *O you who alone are able to do these things for us,*
*and things far more excellent than these —*

*we praise you*
*through the High Priest and Advocate of our souls,*
*Jesus Christ,*
*through whom be the glory and the majesty to you,*
*now and unto all generations,*
*for ever and ever. Amen.*

---

*— SOPHIA*
